newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-BTPs look for gains, but must clear 130-43.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-BTPs look for gains, but must clear 130-43.

text.p: Prospects for June BTP futures traded on LIFFE have improved after Tuesday's reversal from a low of 128.90, technical analysts said on Wednesday.
"Over today I'm looking for a consolidation and then for a push higher," said Robin Wilkin, senior technical analyst at MCM Yieldwatch in London.
"But we need to start clearing 130.20 and 130.43 to consider moving any higher than that," he added. "Otherwise any short term gains still seem corrective."
By 0755 GMT, the June BTP future contract was trading 42 basis points higher on the day at 130.24.
The initial barriers pointed out by Wilkin were the highs on Friday and Thursday last week respectively.

On Tuesday, BTPs came under pressure from a surprise win for the French left on Sunday's first round of parliamentary elections, pushing the June contract down to a two-week low of 128.90 in tandem with weakening bonds across Europe.
The market then pared its losses and resurfaced back above the 130.00 mark.
But the balance above 130.00 is likely to be fragile. Wilkin said any sign of increased selling activity could prompt a move back down towards 128.90.
Below that level, June BTP would face a test of 128.61 -- the 50 percent retracement of the rally from a low of 125.80 on April 25 to the high on May 21 of 131.40.
Further slides would bring into the picture the prospect of 127.92 -- the 62 percent retracement of the same rally.
But technical analysts at an Italian bank in London were also bullish about the near-term outlook.
"The high closing price (on Tuesday), creates expectations for further gains with first target at 130.20 and then 130.55. Good support will be at 129.50," they said in a research note.
June Eurolire was at 93.29, up 0.02 on the day.
